question: Which Fed technology projects are live, and which are only proposed?
answer: Of 17 Fed technology projects the library tracks, 9 are live (FedNow and its add-ons, the Reserve Banks' shared AI platform, Richmond's national IT, the New York repo platform, Philadelphia's collateral systems, Treasury central clearing and DTC's tokenized entitlements), 1 is an authorized but limited account (Kraken), 2 are scheduled (the 2027 FedNow discount and longer Fedwire hours in 2028 or 2029), 2 are proposals (the Payment Account and the Fed's stablecoin rules) and 3 are research only.

items.title: Common Reserve Bank AI platform and workflows
items.sub: AI, data & physical capacity · live — Systemwide internal operation · 2026-02-24
items.text: A common general-purpose platform is available to Reserve Bank employees; hundreds of developers use coding assistants; AI supports regional-intelligence synthesis and is embedded in legal, risk, procurement and operations workflows.
kv: Systemwide direction reported by the Oversight Governor; formal governance instrument is not public.
Named application owner, vendor and platform operator are not publicly stated.
Human decision-makers retain judgment; model, prompt, output and retention records are not publicly mapped.
Official disclosure of all-employee access, hundreds of developer adopters and embedded production workflows.
Use-case descriptions do not prove controlled productivity, application coverage, incident performance or independent assurance.
Platform/vendor identity, use-case and model register, data rules, adoption and outcome metrics, incidents and audit scope.

items.title: FedNow core settlement rail
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · live — scaling · 2026-Q2
items.text: The 24x7 rail recorded nearly five million Q2 customer credit transfers and more than 1,800 live institutions by mid-July.
kv: The twelve Reserve Banks provide the service under Board supervision and pricing approval.
FRFS manages the national business line; current application controller and vendor chain remain incomplete.
Reserve-account settlement under FedNow rules; customer records remain at participating institutions.
4,997,811 Q2 settled transfers worth $274.664 billion; 54,921 average daily transfers.
Participation and volume do not prove send enablement, universal adoption, mature cost recovery or stress resilience.
Q3 volume, send/receive mix, use concentration, uptime/incidents, revenue and application RACI.

items.title: FedNow Network Intelligence API
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · live — bounded early adoption · 2026-04-28
items.text: Network-level receiver-account observations support a sender's pre-payment risk decision through an onboarded API.
kv: FRFS/FedNow operating procedures govern the service.
FRFS/FedNow; early adopters integrate through FedNow onboarding managers or service providers.
FRFS supplies informational insights; the sending institution owns the proceed, hold or review decision.
Launched for early adopters using live FedNow observations.
A score does not stop, settle, reverse or adjudicate a payment and does not prove loss reduction.
Adopter count, model/data governance, false positives, overrides, losses and customer remedy.

items.title: Payee Name Verification
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · live — bounded priced service · 2026
items.text: FedDetect compares payee identity information with Reserve Bank transaction observations before an institution sends a payment.
kv: Operating Circular 5 Appendix E and current service terms.
FRFS through FedLine Direct or FedLine Command.
FRFS returns an informational match result; the originator keeps the payment decision.
Current product and fee schedule charges $0.02 for results other than not found.
Informational matching does not stop or settle a payment and public adoption/error evidence is absent.
Launch/adoption count, match and error distributions, overrides, loss effect and remedy chain.

items.title: Richmond-hosted National IT and procurement
items.sub: AI, data & physical capacity · live operating chassis · 2026-09-30
items.text: ITOC, Richmond National IT, the System CIO and National Procurement provide shared infrastructure, security, budget and selected multi-Bank contracting paths.
kv: System IT policy, Richmond corporate governance and Board/RBOPS oversight remain separate layers.
Richmond-hosted National IT with a geographically distributed workforce.
Application, contract, asset, release and incident ownership is not public as one register.
Current bylaws, committee charter, PFMI disclosures, minutes and inter-Bank reimbursements.
Host location and cost booking do not establish product, software or legal ownership.
ITOC votes, app/vendor register, SLAs, award records, release/incident RACI, remedies and charges.

items.title: Treasury central-clearing implementation
items.sub: Clearing, collateral & settlement · live migration; future mandatory clocks · 2026-12-31 / 2027-06-30
items.text: Market participants and registered clearing agencies are building capacity ahead of cash and repo compliance dates while cleared repo already carries material volume.
kv: FICC plus registered CME Securities Clearing and ICE Clear Credit, with direct members, sponsors and agents.
CCA trade, novation, margin and settlement records; customer and Bank records remain separate.
SEC implementation program and New York Fed evidence of ongoing migration and FICC Sponsored Service scale.
Registration and aggregate migration do not prove participant onboarding, portability, low cost or stress performance.
Compliance receipts, volume by CCA/model, segregation, liquidity, failed novation, concentration and stress outcomes.

items.title: New York SRF and FedTrade Plus
items.sub: Clearing, collateral & settlement · live operation — uncleared · 2025-2026
items.text: Morning operations, removal of the aggregate SRF limit and migration to FedTrade Plus changed live execution while leaving clearing and settlement architecture distinct.
kv: FOMC directive and New York Desk execution.
Federal Reserve Bank of New York Open Market Trading Desk.
SOMA and Desk transaction records across the twelve Bank participation structure.
Live operation under current FOMC implementation terms.
Platform modernization and uncapped aggregate availability do not prove central clearing or wider counterparty rights.
Any directive, rule or operating record assigning a new membership, clearing or settlement configuration.

items.title: DTC tokenized entitlements
items.text: Settled label: LIMITED. DTCC itself called the July 2026 run 'initial, limited production trades' (May 4 release) and the Jul 15 run used DTC's real production environment with real securities for several hours. It is not 'live': DTCC's own page still said 'expected October 2026 launch' when checked on 2026-10-19, and no DTCC announcement of the general launch was found. A KuCoin news flash (Oct 17) says the service launched for 25 securities, citing 'DTCC documentation'; this is unconfirmed.

items.title: Philadelphia collateral and supervisory-data infrastructure
items.sub: Clearing, collateral & settlement · live shared operation; tokenization join unproved · 2026-09-08
items.text: Philadelphia hosts collateral-management, securities-data, RADAR and collaboration functions that could matter to new asset and clearing designs.
kv: Reserve Bank and System governance for the named shared functions.
Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia and named System services.
Application and collateral records exist, but public RACI and technology-product joins are incomplete.
Whole-site recertification establishes current shared operating roles.
Infrastructure and conference attention do not prove a tokenized product or legal-control path.
Application RACI, collateral/legal-control sequence and named production integration.

items.title: Payward/Kraken limited Reserve Bank account
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · Decided 2026-03-04
items.text: Only the Fedwire Funds Service (large-value wire transfers), and only in a way that rejects any payment that would overdraw the account. No intraday credit, no discount-window loans, no interest on balances, and a cap on the end-of-day balance (amount not published). Only Kraken Financial may use it; the Kraken exchange and other Payward companies may not. Initial term of one year. Kraken told Reuters it also has no FedNow or ACH access. As of mid-July 2026 Kraken's CEO said the account was not yet operating; no later public evidence of use was found.

items.title: FedNow 2027 adoption discount
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · scheduled · 2027-01-01
items.text: Statement credits will support receiver enablement and value-added services plus sender enablement and baseline activity.
kv: Customer statement credits and service-usage records.
September 15 announcement with scheduled January 1 start.
A discount is not adoption or incremental volume until institutions qualify and use it.
Final technical terms, qualifying institutions, incremental send volume and cost-recovery effect.

items.title: Fedwire Funds and NSS expanded hours
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · scheduled for 2028 or 2029 · 2028 or 2029
items.text: Future 22x6 central-bank cash settlement will expand Sunday-through-Friday availability with optional participation and a remaining Saturday closure.
kv: FRFS and the twelve Reserve Banks.
Fedwire Funds/NSS settlement records; Fedwire Securities remains separate and excluded.
Scheduled cash hours do not move securities, eliminate weekend gaps or prove participant readiness.
Final year, testing, readiness, launch and any separate Fedwire Securities change.

items.title: National Payment Account, OP-1878
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · Proposed
items.text: Any institution legally eligible for a Reserve Bank account, whatever its tier; an institution could not hold both a Payment Account and a master account. Reserve Banks would decide requests, generally within 90 days of a complete file. The proposal does not widen legal eligibility.

items.title: Board-supervised stablecoin framework
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · Proposed 2026-09-29
items.text: Fed proposes how its member banks apply to issue stablecoins through a subsidiary (R-1900). Fed proposes reserve, capital and redemption standards for the issuers it supervises (R-1899).

items.title: Agentic commerce and AI payments
items.sub: Digital money, payment access & fraud controls · research / industry standards formation · 2026-09-29
items.text: Industry protocols are beginning to address agent identity, delegated authority, approvals, liability, fraud and multi-rail payments.
kv: No new Federal Reserve rail rule or payment-liability regime is established.
Private technology, commerce, card and payment providers; Federal Reserve role is convening and analysis.
Platform and payment-provider records; authoritative consent and liability records remain unresolved.
Public roundtable and speech report early industry development, not Fed deployment.
Questions and private standards do not prove interoperability, legal attribution or production scale.
Named standard adoption, liability rule, production transaction and any Fed rail message/rule change.

items.title: AI power and productivity measurement
items.sub: AI, data & physical capacity · research with measured external constraints · 2026-09-29
items.text: Reserve Bank research joins AI adoption to electricity, interconnection, construction, labor, prices and productivity rather than treating model availability as economic outcome.
kv: Research and monetary-policy sensing; private and public infrastructure actors own the buildout decisions.
Dallas, Minneapolis, San Francisco, Cleveland and Richmond research lanes.
Published papers, surveys and event records; named project operating data remain external.
Dallas estimates current data-center effects on wholesale power prices and frames productivity as the economic test.
Research does not prove energized capacity, realized productivity or Federal Reserve control of the buildout.
Named capacity, utilization, grid delivery, workforce and productivity tied to actual investments.

items.title: Centrally cleared Federal Reserve standing repo
items.sub: Clearing, collateral & settlement · research / staff evaluation · 2026-09-22
items.text: New York Fed officials identify potential monetary-implementation benefits from clearing SRP transactions while staff continue evaluating costs and policy tradeoffs.
kv: Would require FOMC direction plus clearing-agency and Reserve Bank legal/operating arrangements.
No selected operator or membership model beyond current New York Desk execution.
Official advocacy and staff work are not an FOMC directive, CCA membership or live configuration.
FOMC directive, selected CCA/model, filing, contracts, margin/default design, accounting, test and first operation.

uncertain: Four projects (Kraken's account, the Payment Account, the Fed's stablecoin rules and DTC's tokenized entitlements) take their facts from the masters, which are newer; the Fed constellation had the stablecoin proposals on September 24, the master (checked on the web) has September 29.
FedNow's figures are for the second quarter of 2026; the third-quarter figures were not yet published on October 19, 2026.

research.title: Fed Payment Stack Control Finality And Clock Gap
research.answer: There is no single payments stack but five control layers on different clocks. Findings: the clock gap (clearing, guarantee and token hours extend faster than securities-transfer and central-bank cash hours, so private prefunded liquidity bridges the gap)…

research.title: The Fed is many legal bodies, and its building cost doubled
research.answer: The Federal Reserve remains a congressionally created system of Board, FOMC and separately chartered Reserve Banks—not a literal fourth branch—but 2026 doctrine preserves exceptional cause protection for Governors.
